title: Isaiah’s vision concerning Judah
summary: Isaiah’s word concerns Judah and Jerusalem.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw a word concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

unspecified_visual_details: What the vision looks like; whether Isaiah is shown; the setting.

prohibited_inventions: Depicting Isaiah or events in Judah and Jerusalem as physically present without textual description.

title: Nations flow to the Lord’s house
summary: In the last days, the Lord’s house is established above the hills, and nations flow to it. People invite one another to go there to learn the Lord’s ways.

explicit_facts.text: In the last days, the mountain of the Lord’s house is established in the top of the mountains and exalted above the hills; all nations flow unto it.
Many people say to come to the mountain of the Lord and the house of the God of Jacob to be taught his ways and walk in his paths.
The law goes forth from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People traveling toward a high mountain and gathering there.
unspecified_visual_details: The mountain’s appearance, architecture, era, and the identities and appearance of the people.

spoken_dialogue.text: Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Many people

prohibited_inventions: Depicting God or Jacob as physically present; inventing a named temple or particular people.

title: Weapons become tools
summary: He shall judge among the nations and rebuke many people. They shall beat their swords into plow-shares and their spears into pruning-hooks. Nations shall not lift up swords against one another or learn war any more.

explicit_facts.text: He shall judge among the nations and rebuke many people.
They shall beat their swords into plow-shares and their spears into pruning-hooks.
Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn war any more.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People reshaping swords and spears into agricultural tools.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's appearance, the location, the tools' design, and the manner of judgment or rebuke.

narration.text: and they shall beat their swords into plow-shares, and their spears into pruning-hooks—nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes a future cessation of war.
prohibited_inventions: A battle or a visible appearance for the unnamed judge.
Invented speech or a specific setting.

title: Call to walk in the Lord’s light
summary: The house of Jacob is called to walk in the light of the Lord and told that all have gone astray to wicked ways.

explicit_facts.text: The house of Jacob is called to walk in the light of the Lord.
The house of Jacob is told that all have gone astray, every one to his wicked ways.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s identity and appearance, the hearers’ appearance, and the setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: O house of Jacob, come ye and let us walk in the light of the Lord; yea, come, for ye have all gone astray, every one to his wicked ways.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is an exhortation, not a narrated gathering or a literal depiction of light.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing a speaker or depicting the house of Jacob as a specific visible group.

title: The house of Jacob’s practices
summary: The Lord has forsaken the house of Jacob. Their land is full of silver, gold, treasures, horses, chariots, and idols, and they worship what they have made.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord has forsaken the house of Jacob because they are replenished from the east, hearken to soothsayers like the Philistines, and please themselves in the children of strangers.
Their land is full of silver, gold, treasures, horses, and chariots.
Their land is full of idols, and they worship what their own hands and fingers have made.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Silver, gold, horses, chariots, and idols may be shown in the land.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the people, landscape, chariots, and idols.

narration.text: Therefore, O Lord, thou hast forsaken thy people, the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and hearken unto soothsayers like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children of strangers.
Their land is also full of idols;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses describe conditions and practices rather than a particular encounter or sequence of actions.
prohibited_inventions: A specific soothsaying, encounter with strangers’ children, or idol-making event.

title: The unhumble are condemned

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not narrate a distinct act of punishment.

title: Warning to the wicked
summary: A warning calls on the wicked to hide in rock and dust and foretells that the proud will be brought low and the Lord alone exalted.

explicit_facts.text: The wicked are told to enter the rock and hide in the dust for fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty.
The lofty looks and haughtiness of people will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted in that day.
The day of the Lord of Hosts is said to be coming upon all nations and every person; the proud and lofty will be brought low.

unspecified_visual_details: Who, if anyone, delivers the warning aloud.

narration.text: O ye wicked ones, enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust,
and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
For the day of the Lord of Hosts soon cometh upon all nations, yea, upon every one;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The humbling and exaltation are prophetic statements, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Assigning the warning to Isaiah or presenting it as confirmed spoken dialogue.

title: The day of the Lord upon the lofty
summary: The prophecy names the cedars of Lebanon, oaks of Bashan, high mountains and hills, lifted-up nations and every people, high towers and fenced walls, ships of the sea and Tarshish, and pleasant pictures as subject to the day of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The day of the Lord shall come upon the cedars of Lebanon and the oaks of Bashan.

The prophecy includes every high tower and fenced wall.
The prophecy includes ships of the sea, ships of Tarshish, and pleasant pictures.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the ships, towers, walls, and pleasant pictures.

title: The Lord alone exalted
summary: The verses foretell that human loftiness and haughtiness will be made low, the Lord alone will be exalted, and idols will be abolished.

explicit_facts.text: The loftiness of man shall be bowed down, the haughtiness of men shall be made low, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
The idols shall be utterly abolished.

unspecified_visual_details: How the prophetic humbling and abolition of idols are represented visually.

narration.text: and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic statements; no visible appearance of the Lord or specific act of idol-abolition is described.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting the Lord's appearance or a specific physical event of idol-abolition.

title: A Prophetic Day Among the Rocks
summary: The verses foretell people going into holes and caves, and into clefts and the tops of ragged rocks, when fear of the Lord comes upon them and he arises to shake the earth. In that day, a man casts the silver and gold idols he made for worship to the moles and bats.
